sonnet.problem: The question asks what the eagle picture shows, and the right answer ('There was no escaping them') is a meaning the passage never states. Verse 19 only says the pursuers were swifter than eagles.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: The card calls the LORD's anointed 'the king'. Verse 20 never says this, so the card adds an identification the text leaves open. It also calls it 'another painful loss', which is the card's own claim and not marked as Papa Dorin's guess.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The question says the people 'had high hopes' for the anointed. The text gives only what they said, 'Under his shadow we will live among the nations', and not how they felt. This feeling is stated as fact and not marked as a guess.
sonnet.rule: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'Edom is rejoicing now'. Verse 21 gives a command ('So rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom'), not a report that Edom is rejoicing. The question stretches the text.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The question says the elders 'find no favor', and card 6 just said 'He regards them no more'. Together these make the wrong answers ('praised for their service', 'welcomed by the nations') obviously false, so the setup gives the answer away.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
